t: You're looking at the London Hilton on Park Lane, a tall hotel on Park Lane, overlooking Hyde Park, in exclusive Mayfair. It stands a hundred metres high, with twenty-eight storeys and four hundred and fifty-three rooms, fifty-six of them suites. The architect was William B. Tabler, an American who designed more than four hundred hotels. He was best known for giving Hilton hotels the clean, sometimes stark face of corporate America, most notably in the New York Hilton Midtown. This tower is part of that same story.
